full_judgment:
6. Ms. Syeda Anowara Sattar, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents No.2 to 4 submitted that under the Hindu Law, even in the case of a minor who is married, the custody will go to her husband and in this case an application has been filed by the father-in-law of the victim for her custody. She submits that under the definition of a child as found in section 2(f) of the Children Act, 1974, anyone under the age of 16 is a child. She points out that the school record and the official documentation relating to the victim's S.S.C. registration shows that at the relevant time she was above the age of the 16 and, therefore, being a major she should not be held in safe custody and should be released to go whosesoever she pleases. In this regard she refers to the decision in the case of Rehana Begum and another Vs. Govt. of Bangladesh and others, 18 BLD 410. 

 9. On 22.11.2009, we spoke to Kanamika @ Kona Shaha in the Chamber of the presiding Judge in the presence of the learned advocates, representing the appellant as well as the respondents and also the learned Assistant Attorney General, Dr. Md. Bashir Ullah. From her statement before us it transpired that Kanamika ® Kona Shaha sat for her S.S.C. Examination in 2009 and achieved grade-A. Her S.S.C. Admit Card shows her date of birth as 01.04.1993. She told us that she was initially kept in safe custody at the Laxmipur Jail for about three months and, thereafter, transferred on 05.08.2009 to the Safe Home in Farhadabad, Hathazari, Chittagong. She told us that she voluntarily ran away from home and married Prabir Deb Nath on 15.03.2009 and, thereafter, went to the house of her husband's sister, who lives in Patuakhali, where their marriage was consummated and they remained there for 15/16 days and thereafter she came home on the assurance given by her mother that her marriage would be accepted. But on her return she was apprehended by the police. She told us that her parents would not consent to her marriage to her husband particularly since she has an elder sister who is still unmarried and it was the elder sister, who, on her return home, physically and verbally abused and assaulted her. When asked whether she would go back to the family home, she categorically refused to go, because of the fact that she was assaulted by her sister and she feared that because her sister was still unmarried she would again assault her. We noted that she did not allege any assault by her parents. We may mention that, thereafter, we talked to the victim girl in the presence of her parents when again she refused to go back home stating that her sister would assault her. We noted that the parents, although they stated that they would not in any way assault and abuse her, did not protest against the allegation that the victim's sister had assaulted her. 

 12. In her further submissions before this Court learned advocate Ms. Syeda Anwara Sattar submitted that according to Hindu Law the husband is the lawful guardian of his minor wife. She also pointed out that according to the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1966 (an Indian Statute), section 6(c) states that in the case of a married girl the natural guardian is the husband. She also pointed out from the commentary in Showkat Mahmood's "Guardian and Wards Act and Majority Act" that under Hindu Law a Hindu girl aged 17 is a major under the Hindu Law in respect of marriage and she can marry without the consent of the guardian of her person. The learned advocate submitted that the husband being the legal guardian, the victim girl was bound to be placed in his custody, but since he was himself in jail custody, the custody of the girl may be given to the father of the husband or alternatively to the custody of BNWLA for her better education till the release of her husband from jail custody. 

 19. This measure is for the interim period between now and the date when the girl reaches the age of 18 years. At this stage we will not advert to the possibility that the husband may make any application for his wife's custody if and when he is released from jail within this period. It appears to us that the Hindu Law is clear and the husband may do as he may be advised. But so far as the welfare of the girl is concerned, we would like to ensure, after having passed this order, that she will not be assaulted or abused by any members of the family and that she will have recourse to the educational facilities. In that regard we have asked Ms. Syeda Anwara Sattar, learned advocate who is a member of the BNWLA, that she will monitor the progress of the girl by arranging a visit to the residence of the appellant to find out the progress of Kanamika @ Kona Shaha after six months from date and report compliance to the Registrar of this Court.
